$comment: Conformance vectors for text/event-stream. Generated from wire/conformance_test.go; do not edit by hand.

vectors.name: terminator/lf
vectors.why: A lone line feed terminates a line.

vectors.name: terminator/crlf
vectors.why: A CRLF pair terminates a line and counts as one terminator.

vectors.name: terminator/cr
vectors.why: A lone carriage return terminates a line. Libraries that split only on LF are incorrect here.

vectors.name: terminator/mixed
vectors.why: Terminators may be mixed freely within one stream.
vectors.input:
data: a
data: bdata: c

vectors.name: bom/stripped
vectors.why: UTF-8 decoding strips one leading byte order mark.

vectors.name: bom/only-one
vectors.why: Only the first byte order mark is stripped; a second one is part of the field name and makes it unknown.

vectors.name: space/absent
vectors.why: No space after the colon means no space is removed.

vectors.name: space/one
vectors.why: Exactly one leading space is removed.

vectors.name: space/two
vectors.why: Only one space is removed, so the second survives. This is why an encoder must always write the space: doing it conditionally eats a character from any payload starting with one.

vectors.name: data/empty-value-dispatches
vectors.why: A data field with an empty value leaves a line feed in the buffer, so the buffer is not empty and the event IS dispatched with empty data. Only a block with no data field at all is suppressed.

vectors.name: data/absent-suppresses
vectors.why: A block carrying only an event field has an empty data buffer and is suppressed.

vectors.name: data/multiline
vectors.why: Repeated data fields are rejoined with line feeds.

vectors.name: data/trailing-blank-line-preserved
vectors.why: Only the final line feed is stripped, so a payload can end in one.

vectors.name: data/no-colon-is-empty-value
vectors.why: A line with no colon is the field name with an empty value, so a bare 'data' line appends an empty line.

vectors.name: id/without-data-advances-cursor
vectors.why: The last event ID is committed before the empty-data check, so an id-only block advances the client's cursor while dispatching nothing. This is the primitive that makes out-of-band checkpointing free.

vectors.name: id/persists-across-events
vectors.why: The id buffer is never reset by a dispatch, so a later event with no id inherits the previous one.

vectors.name: id/empty-resets-cursor
vectors.why: An empty id field sets the cursor to the empty string, so the client sends no Last-Event-ID on its next reconnection. It is the specification's own way to say a stored position is no longer resolvable.
vectors.input:
data: a
id: 1

data: b
id

vectors.name: id/nul-ignored
vectors.why: An id containing NUL makes the client ignore the whole field, leaving the cursor where it was.

vectors.name: retry/digits
vectors.why: A value of only ASCII digits sets the reconnection time in milliseconds.

vectors.name: retry/non-numeric-ignored
vectors.why: Anything that is not only ASCII digits is ignored.

vectors.name: retry/fractional-ignored
vectors.why: A decimal point is not an ASCII digit, so the field is ignored entirely rather than truncated.

vectors.name: retry/signed-ignored
vectors.why: A sign is not an ASCII digit.

vectors.name: field/unknown-ignored
vectors.why: Unknown field names are ignored.

vectors.name: field/case-sensitive
vectors.why: Field names are compared literally, with no case folding, so 'Data' is an unknown field.

vectors.name: comment/ignored
vectors.why: A line starting with a colon is a comment.

vectors.name: comment/only-dispatches-nothing
vectors.why: A block of only comments has an empty data buffer and is suppressed. This is what makes a comment a zero-cost keep-alive.

vectors.name: event/named
vectors.why: An event field sets the dispatched type.

vectors.name: event/resets-between-blocks
vectors.why: The event type buffer is reset on dispatch, so a later block with no event field is a plain message.
vectors.input:
event: token
data: a

data: b

vectors.name: event/reset-even-when-suppressed
vectors.why: The event type buffer is also cleared when a block is suppressed for carrying no data.

vectors.name: eof/incomplete-block-discarded
vectors.why: Dispatch happens on a blank line, and end of file is not one. A final block without its blank line is dropped, which is why a graceful shutdown must close the last block.

vectors.name: eof/partial-line-discarded
vectors.why: A line with no terminator at end of file is discarded.

vectors.name: spec/four-block-example
vectors.why: The four-block example from the WHATWG specification, end to end: a comment that fires nothing, an event that sets the cursor to 1, an event that resets the cursor, and an event whose payload keeps a leading space.
